title: Deterministic correlation ID stitching and log coalescer
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Goal: implement a resilient ingestion component that deterministically stitches together partial correlation identifiers across heterogeneous producers and coalesces semantically-related log events into single logical records for downstream Loki and ELK sinks.

Why: We've observed tail-latency and diagnostic gaps when services emit fragmented identifiers or use nonstandard JSON shapes. This ticket builds a middleware step that: 1) creates stable, deterministic correlation IDs when partially-present fields exist (trace_id, span_id, request_id, x-corr headers); 2) normalizes common vendor/event shapes into a compact canonical envelope; 3) coalesces small, high-frequency event fragments (e.g., debug lines, incremental state diffs) into bounded batched records to reduce cardinality and downstream indexing costs without losing ordering semantics.

Scope:
- Parser layer that accepts jsonl, plain text, and proto-style payloads and applies a lightweight shape classifier.
- Deterministic stitching rules: prefer explicit trace_id if present, otherwise synthesize using stable hash over (tenant_id, service, timestamp-window, local_id). Hash must be stable across restarts and use our existing tenant key salt.
- Coalescer with configurable time window (default 250ms) and size cap (default 16 events); emits unified envelope with ordered fragments and retention metadata.
- Tenant-aware routing: coalesced records should preserve tenant shard keys for Kafka partitioning.
- Backpressure behavior: when queue depths exceed threshold, fallback to pass-through (no coalescing) with a dropped-fragments metric emitted.

Acceptance criteria:
- End-to-end tests that validate deterministic ID generation across simulated restarts and across two different producers emitting complementary fragments.
- Benchmark shows <=5% added P50 ingest latency at our 95th percentile load profile and >=30% reduction in average downstream index write rate for a synthetic fragment-heavy workload.
- No change to existing trace linkage in traces -> logs integrations; UI trace links still surface the new correlation IDs.
- Feature flag gated and rolloutable per-tenant via console.

Migration and rollout plan:
1) Feature-gated deploy to canary cluster (internal tenants) and metric verification (3 days).
2) Gradual rollout to 10% of tenants by tenant load class, monitor dropped-fragments, and latency dashboards.
3) If dropped-fragments > 0.5% or ingest P95 increases by >8%, rollback.

Observability for this work:
- New metrics: coalescer.window_ms, coalescer.coalesced_count, coalescer.dropped_fragments, coalescer.synthetic_id_rate, coalescer.pass_through_rate.
- Logs: coalescer.lifecycle events with reason-coded drops.
- Dashboards: per-tenant coalescer health, sample of coalesced envelopes, and correlation ID lineage view.

Security notes: deterministic hashing uses tenant key salt from KMS; KMS access must be validated by Security prior to canary.
